title: Diabetic kidney disease (India)
specialty: Nephrology / Endocrinology / Internal Medicine / Primary Care

evidenceAudit.scope: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) caused by type 2 diabetes in adults in India: screening, staging by eGFR and albuminuria, renoprotection with ACE inhibitors or ARBs and SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin dosing by eGFR, glycaemic targets, diet and referral, using KDIGO 2022 with ICMR Type 2 Diabetes and Cardiology workflows for Indian practice and doses.
findings: ACE inhibitor or ARB at the highest tolerated dose with albuminuria (1.2.1), SGLT2 inhibitor for eGFR 20 or more (1.3.1), non-steroidal MRA for eGFR 25 or more with albuminuria 30 mg/g or more (1.4.1), metformin for eGFR 30 or more with dose halved at 30–44 and stopped below 30 (Figure 27), HbA1c targets below 6.5% to below 8.0% (2.2.1), protein 0.8 g/kg/day (3.1.1), sodium below 2 g/day (3.1.2), creatinine and potassium check 2–4 weeks after RAS changes and SGLT2 sick-day rules checked against KDIGO 2022.
Annual urine ACR and creatinine from the ICMR Type 2 Diabetes STW; ramipril and enalapril doses from the ICMR Cardiology STW; dapagliflozin 10 mg and eGFR thresholds from its US label.
unverifiedSections: Finerenone dose was not in the opened KDIGO extract and is not dosed here.
A specific BP target was not in the opened KDIGO extract; the ICMR Hypertension STW target below 130/80 mmHg for diabetes or CKD is used.
The metformin maximum dose is not stated in the opened extract.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Diabetic kidney disease develops in many people with long-standing type 2 diabetes and is a leading cause of kidney failure in India. Hyperglycaemia, glomerular hyperfiltration and hypertension damage the glomeruli, first causing albuminuria and later a falling eGFR. Because it is silent, everyone with diabetes needs yearly urine albumin-creatinine ratio (ACR) and creatinine (ICMR STW). Four treatments slow progression and reduce cardiovascular events: an ACE inhibitor or ARB at the highest tolerated dose when albuminuria is present, an SGLT2 inhibitor when eGFR is 20 or more, metformin adjusted to eGFR, and control of BP, lipids, smoking and salt (KDIGO 2022).
keyMechanisms: Hyperglycaemia and advanced glycation damage the glomerular basement membrane and podocytes.
Glomerular hyperfiltration raises intraglomerular pressure, causing albuminuria.
RAS blockade and SGLT2 inhibition lower intraglomerular pressure.
Progressive sclerosis lowers eGFR and leads to kidney failure.

symptoms: Fatigue, nausea, itch in advanced CKD
redFlags: Rapid eGFR fall or sudden rise in proteinuria: look for another cause
Potassium above 5.5 mmol/L on RAS blockade
Haematuria or active urinary sediment: non-diabetic disease
precipitants: Long diabetes duration, poor glucose control

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Haematuria, red cell casts, rapid change.
Agricultural areas, no diabetes; see CKD topic.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Urine ACR 30 mg/g (3 mg/mmol) or more on repeat testing.
eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² or albuminuria for over 3 months.
60 or more: usual dose; 45–59: continue, reduce in some; 30–44: halve; below 30: stop.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Annual in diabetes (ICMR STW); albuminuria triggers RAS blockade (KDIGO 1.2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Screen
actions: Urine ACR and creatinine yearly in diabetes (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Renoprotection
actions: ACE inhibitor or ARB titrated to the highest tolerated dose (KDIGO 1.2.1).
Check creatinine and potassium in 2–4 weeks; continue unless creatinine rises over 30% (KDIGO 1.2.2–1.2.3).
SGLT2 inhibitor if eGFR 20 or more; continue below 20 if already started (KDIGO 1.3.1, 1.3.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Glucose control
actions: Metformin if eGFR 30 or more, dosed by eGFR (KDIGO 4.1.1).
Add a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist if targets not met (KDIGO 4.2.1).
HbA1c target below 6.5% to below 8.0% by individual risk (KDIGO 2.2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Risk factors and diet
actions: Protein 0.8 g/kg/day; sodium below 2 g/day; 150 minutes activity a week (KDIGO 3.1–3.2).

clinicalManagement.title: Sick-day rules and referral
actions: Withhold SGLT2 inhibitor in acute illness, reduced intake or 3 days before surgery (dapagliflozin label; KDIGO).
Refer to nephrology for eGFR below 30, rapid decline or atypical features.

branches.label: Renoprotection
branches.entryCriteria: Diabetes with CKD and albuminuria or eGFR 20 or more.

regimens.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg (highest tolerated)
adjustments: Paediatric: Adult topic; paediatric use is outside the scope of the cited sources.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Check creatinine and potassium 2–4 weeks after each change; continue unless creatinine rises over 30% (KDIGO).

regimens.useWhen: Ramipril unavailable; use an ARB (for example telmisartan) if ACE-inhibitor cough.

regimens.patientGroup: Adults with eGFR 25 or more to start
regimens.duration: Long term; continue if eGFR later falls below 20 (KDIGO 1.3.6)
adjustments: Paediatric: Not established for this indication in children.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Do not start if eGFR below 25 (label); KDIGO: start if 20 or more.
contraindications: Withhold in acute illness or 3 days before surgery (ketoacidosis risk)

regimens.dose: eGFR 60 or more: usual dose; 45–59: continue, reduce in some; 30–44: halve the dose; below 30: stop
adjustments: Paediatric: Adult topic; paediatric use is outside the scope of the cited sources.
Penicillin allergy: Not an antibiotic; penicillin allergy does not change this medicine.
CKD: Dose by eGFR (KDIGO Figure 27); monitor eGFR more often below 60.
CLD: Avoid in liver failure (lactic acidosis).
monitoring: eGFR at least every 3–6 months below 60
contraindications: Acute illness with dehydration or hypoxia

medicationPlan.note: Treatment framework from KDIGO 2022; ACE inhibitor doses from the ICMR Cardiology STW; dapagliflozin from its US label. Finerenone and GLP-1 receptor agonists are options but not dosed here. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Screen with urine ACR and eGFR yearly.
Adjust metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors to eGFR.
keyPoints: ACR 30 mg/g or more: ACEi or ARB to highest tolerated dose.
SGLT2 inhibitor if eGFR 20 or more.
Metformin halved at eGFR 30–44, stopped below 30.
Check potassium and creatinine 2–4 weeks after RAS changes.
pitfalls: Stopping ACEi for a small creatinine rise.
